html:
The Honduran general strike of 1954 was a strike of banana workers on the north coast, against the United Fruit Company and Standard Fruit, from May to July 1954. Tens of thousands stopped work.

Workers had no unions and earned little, and the strike spread from the docks of Tela to the plantations and towns of the region. It was the largest labour action in the history of Honduras. It came as the United States was organising the coup in Guatemala next door, and the government feared communist influence.

The strike ended with pay rises and the right to organise. Unions became a lasting force, a labour code followed in 1959, and the strike is remembered as the moment the banana republic began to change.
